error.signature: AI tells a traveler it's fine to bring small, personal-use quantities of meat, milk, or dairy products into Belgium in their luggage from a non-EU/non-EEA-equivalent country

verdict.summary: Belgium's federal food safety agency (FASFC) and the European Commission's official personal-imports guidance, under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122, state that travellers 'are not allowed to bring in meat, milk or their products' into the EU from third countries - an outright ban with no personal-use or small-quantity threshold. Narrow exceptions exist: up to 2 kg of unopened, non-refrigerated infant formula or medical foods; up to 20 kg of fish/fishery products; up to 2 kg of honey, eggs, or live shellfish/snails; and a full exemption for goods from Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, San Marino, or Switzerland (plus a 10 kg meat/dairy allowance from the Faeroe Islands or Greenland).

dead_ends.action: Tell a traveler that bringing a small amount of homemade cheese, cured meat, or other dairy/meat product from a non-EU country (outside Andorra/Iceland/Liechtenstein/Norway/San Marino/Switzerland) into Belgium in personal luggage is fine, or just needs to be declared
dead_ends.why_fails: FASFC's own guidance and the European Commission's official personal-imports page both state travellers 'are not allowed to bring in meat, milk or their products' from third countries at all, under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122 - it is a flat ban, not a declare-and-pass rule or a duty/quantity threshold, regardless of the amount or that it's for personal consumption.
dead_ends.condition: Meat or dairy product from a non-EU/non-exempt country

dead_ends.action: Assume the same total ban applies to fish, honey, eggs, or infant formula brought from outside the EU
dead_ends.why_fails: The same EU regulation sets separate, more generous allowances for other animal-origin foods: up to 20 kg of fish/fishery products, up to 2 kg of honey/eggs/live shellfish/snails, and up to 2 kg of unopened, non-refrigerated infant formula or medical foods - these categories are not covered by the meat/dairy ban.
dead_ends.condition: Fish, honey, eggs, or infant/medical foods rather than meat or dairy
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the rule bans all animal-origin food, when it specifically targets meat and dairy, with separate and more generous limits for other animal-origin foods.

workarounds.action: Before traveling to Belgium from a non-EU, non-exempt country, leave meat and dairy products behind (or consume them before arrival); for goods from Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, the Faeroe Islands, or Greenland, or for fish/honey/eggs/infant-medical foods, check the specific exemption and weight limit first
workarounds.condition: Traveling to Belgium with animal-origin food from outside the EU
